'''Marlies Gerber''' is an American mathematician whose research applies [[descriptive set theory]] to [[dynamical system]]s. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Indiana University Bloomington]].{{r|icm}}

==Education and career==
Gerber was the 1971 [[salutatorian]] of [[Zephyrhills High School]] in Florida.{{r|zh}} As an undergraduate at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]], Gerber competed with [[Bruce Hajek]] and [[Daniel Sleator]] in the 1974 [[Putnam Competition]], winning an honorable mention for their team.{{r|putnam}} At the University of Illinois, Gerber was the 1974 recipient of the H. Roy Brahana Prize for the "student with the most exceptional undergraduate mathematics career".{{r|brahana}}

Gerber completed her Ph.D. in 1979 at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. Her dissertation, ''Topics in Ergodic Theory'', was supervised by Jacob Feldman.{{r|mg}} She became a postdoctoral scholar at the [[University of Maryland]] and then a faculty member at Indiana University Bloomington.{{r|icm}} In 1982, when she joined Indiana University, the mathematics department had only one other woman on its faculty, and there were many years when she was the department's only tenured or tenure-track woman.{{r|under}}

==Recognition==
Gerber was an invited speaker at the 2026 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], on her work with Philipp Kunde proving that [[isomorphism]] of [[diffeomorphism|smooth]] [[ergodic flow]]s forms a [[binary relation]] that cannot be described as a [[Borel set]]. This work resolves negatively a problem of classifying these flows posed in 1932 by [[John von Neumann]].{{r|icm}}
